The closest match is a set of papers on low-precision training for large language models, but not specifically on private devices. One paper studies FP4 pretraining recipes and shows how selective high-precision layers and improved gradient handling help recover accuracy at scale [1]. Another proposes adaptive block scaling for NVFP4 to reduce quantization error and improve training loss, and a third presents stable FP4 training with transposition-invariant block quantization that closely matches BF16 [2, 3].

For distributed training efficiency, AGoQ focuses on memory-efficient distributed LLM training with 4-bit activations and 8-bit gradients, improving speed on GPU clusters [7]. None of the supplied papers directly addresses low-precision training across distributed private devices; the closest privacy-related paper is about differentially private fine-tuning, but it does not study low-precision numbers for distributed devices [6].
